title: [BUG-06] Predictive Models — BAU and Target Range lines flip / tooltip shows incorrect values when single model selected
description:
In the Predictive Models section on the Performance Overview, the BAU (predicted) line and the Target Range line display incorrectly when a single model is selected. The issue does NOT appear when 'All Models' is selected — only when filtered to a single model (e.g. Web only).

OBSERVED ON: ClassPass account (unified model)

STEPS TO REPRODUCE:
1. Open Performance Overview for ClassPass
2. Select all models — observe Predictive Models chart (note correct display)
3. Change filter to a single model (e.g. Web)
4. Observe the BAU line and Target Range line on the chart
5. Hover over the chart to see the tooltip

ACTUAL RESULT:
- The Target Range line appears HIGHER than the BAU (blue dotted) line on the chart
- However the tooltip shows the Target Range as LOWER — the opposite of what the chart displays
- The line chart and the tooltip are showing contradictory information
- The two lines appear to flip / swap their axis assignments when switching from All Models to a single model filter

EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR:
- The tooltip must always correctly identify which line is BAU and which is Target Range
- The values shown in the tooltip must match the visual position of the lines on the chart
- Switching between All Models and single model filter must not cause the lines or their labels to swap

NOTE: Screenshot available from Gary Danks — request before investigating.
NOTE: May be specific to ClassPass as a unified model — check whether this occurs on other accounts.

Type: Bug | Priority: Critical | Area: Performance Overview → Predictive Models
Reported by: Gary Danks — 6 May 2026

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-01] Allow drag-and-drop reordering of Metrics & KPI tiles and Predictive Model tiles
description:
Users cannot currently reorder Metrics & KPI tiles or Predictive Model tiles. The order is fixed after creation. This limits the client's ability to prioritise the metrics that matter most to them.

Proposed fix: Add drag-and-drop reordering for both Metrics & KPI tiles and Predictive Model tiles.

Rule: Ad Spend should always be the first Metrics & KPI tile by default and should be fixed/pinned in position one. All other tiles can be reordered freely.

Implementation notes: Use a standard drag handle icon on the left or top-left of each tile. Order should persist after save. Consider a subtle 'drag to reorder' tooltip on first use.

Type: New feature | Priority: High | Area: Performance Overview

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-06] Cost curve charts look too lightweight — needs more visual rigour
description:
The cost curve charts do not visually convey the scientific credibility and analytical depth of the underlying model. Feedback: 'like a PowerPoint presentation.'

Proposed fix: Improve the visual design of cost curve charts to increase perceived analytical rigour. This does not mean adding unnecessary complexity — it means the charts should feel like they belong in a professional data science product, not a slide deck. Specific improvements TBD in design review.

Type: Design improvement | Priority: High | Area: Cost Curve

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-05] Reframe attribution column copy — make clear these are directional MMM estimates, not LTA comparisons
description:
The current attribution column framing is causing client friction. Clients are comparing AIM attribution figures directly against last-touch attribution (LTA) figures from their MMP, which leads to confusion and loss of confidence in the model.

Proposed fix: Reframe all copy and tooltips in the attribution column to make clear that these are directional MMM estimates — not a like-for-like comparison with LTA. This is a copy and tooltip fix — not a data change.

NOTE: This is causing active client friction now. Priority item.

Type: New feature (copy/UX) | Priority: CRITICAL | Area: Sources / Media Partners

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-02] Add model health and provenance signals to Performance Overview (MAPE, last updated, last attribution run)
description:
The Performance Overview currently shows outputs but no information about the model that generated them. Clients have no visibility into how accurate the model is, when it was last updated, or when attribution data was last run.

Proposed additions — add the following contextual signals to the Performance Overview header or model info panel:
- MAPE Score: The model's Mean Absolute Percentage Error — displayed alongside the date it was calculated
- Model Last Updated: Date and time the model was last rebuilt/retrained
- Last Attribution Run: Date and time of the most recent attribution data run

Example format: 'Model accuracy (MAPE): 8.4% (calculated 28 Apr 2026) | Last model update: 29 Apr 2026 14:32 | Last attribution run: 30 Apr 2026 09:17'

These are read-only provenance indicators that materially increase client confidence and reduce 'is this fresh?' support questions.

Type: New feature | Priority: High | Area: Performance Overview → header

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-06] Add persistent active filter display bar to all pages — cadence and lookback window
description:
Users have no at-a-glance view of which filters are currently applied. After selecting cadence and lookback window there is no persistent on-screen indicator.

PROPOSED SOLUTION:
Add a persistent filter bar near the top of all pages showing active filters as labelled pill/chip buttons.

Example:
[ Monthly ] [ Last 12 Months ] [ All Platforms ] [ All Networks ]

Design requirements:
- Pill/chip button style — not plain text
- Each chip clearly labelled with its current value
- Clicking a chip opens the relevant filter selector inline
- Updates immediately when filters change
- Must include at minimum: cadence + lookback window. Platform and network filters should also appear here.

Type: New feature | Priority: High | Area: Global — all pages, specifically Performance Overview and Media Partners
Reported by: Gary Danks — 6 May 2026

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-07] Redesign date filter UX — split into two explicit selectors + reduce calendar to icon
description:
The current date filter UI is unclear. The full calendar button takes up too much space and the relationship between cadence and lookback window is not obvious.

PROPOSED REDESIGN:

1. CADENCE SELECTOR — segmented toggle:
   Monthly | Weekly | Custom

2. LOOKBACK WINDOW SELECTOR — adjacent dropdown or segmented selector showing options relevant to the selected cadence:
   - Monthly: Last 12 Months | Last 9 Months | Last 6 Months | Custom Range
   - Weekly: Last 52 Weeks | Last 26 Weeks | Last 13 Weeks | Custom Range
   - Custom: Custom Range only

3. CALENDAR — reduce to a small calendar icon. When clicked, opens the existing calendar overlay (same behaviour as today, smaller trigger). Only needed for custom date range selection.

This is a UI redesign only — no change to underlying date logic or data.

Combined with FEATURE-06 (persistent filter bar), the user will always know exactly what they are looking at.

Type: New feature / UX redesign | Priority: High | Area: Global — date filter / cadence selector
Reported by: Gary Danks — 6 May 2026

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-09] Recommendations / Optimizer — Add optimizer summary header with KPI target and last run date
description:
The Recommendations section currently lists recommendations with no context about what the optimizer is working towards or when it last ran. Two additions required.

---

CHANGES REQUIRED:

1. OPTIMIZER TARGET SUMMARY
- Add a summary statement at the top of the Recommendations section, above individual recommendation rows
- Must clearly state what KPI the optimizer is currently optimising towards
- Example: 'Currently optimising towards: Paid Subscriptions'
- Must be dynamically pulled from the client's model configuration — not hardcoded
- Will differ per client (e.g. 'Subscriptions' for ClassPass, 'First Time Deposits' for fintech, etc.)

2. OPTIMIZER LAST RUN DATE AND TIME
- Display the date and time the optimizer last ran, adjacent to or below the target summary
- Example: 'Optimizer last run: 5 May 2026 at 22:00'
- Must include a timestamp — date alone is not sufficient
- Must be clearly distinguished from the Model Refresh Date (see FEATURE-08)

---

DESIGN INTENT:
- Compact, positioned at top of Recommendations section — first thing user reads before acting on any recommendation
- Should feel like a live system status panel, not a marketing message
- Gives the user confidence that recommendations are current and reflect the latest model run

---

Type: New feature | Priority: High
Area: Recommendations / Optimizer → section header
Reported by: Gary Danks — 6 May 2026

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-08] Performance Overview — Add Model Performance section above Metrics & KPIs
description:
A new 'Model Performance' section is required at the very top of the Performance Overview page, positioned ABOVE the existing Metrics & KPI tiles. This section gives users immediate confidence that their model is live, accurate, and up to date.

---

CONTENT REQUIRED:

1. MAPE SCORE
- Display the current MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error) score
- Show as a colour-coded badge with a performance label:
  • Excellent → Green
  • Good → Yellow-green
  • Standard → Amber
  • Poor → Red
  (Exact thresholds to be confirmed with Robert / Data Science)
- Display the date and time the MAPE was recorded alongside the score
- MAPE updates daily — show today's date if available. If not, must be no more than 7 days ago.

2. MODEL REFRESH DATE
- Date and time the model was last rebuilt / retrained
- Target: within last 7 days
- Format: 'Last refreshed: 5 May 2026 at 14:32'

3. LAST ATTRIBUTION RUN
- Date and time of the most recent attribution data run
- Runs daily — should reflect the most recent run
- Format: 'Last attribution run: 6 May 2026 at 09:17'

---

DESIGN INTENT:
- Must look scientific and data-driven — feels like it is pulled live from the backend
- Conveys recency and freshness — user should feel their model is current and active
- MAPE badge colour must be immediately legible without reading the label
- Do not use decorative or marketing-style design — this is a technical provenance panel

---

Type: New feature | Priority: High
Area: Performance Overview → top of page, above Metrics & KPIs
Reported by: Gary Danks — 6 May 2026

3. Scroll down the table

This is a usability issue affecting all clients with more than a small number of networks in their media mix.

Type: UX fix | Priority: High
Area: Media Partners → main table → column headers

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-01] Overall visual language feels too lightweight — all pages
description:
The current AIM Insights interface is too clean and minimal. It does not visually convey the sophistication of the underlying Bayesian model. Clients who see it for the first time may not appreciate the level of statistical rigour behind the outputs.

Proposed fix: Review the overall visual design with the goal of increasing perceived analytical depth. This does not mean adding clutter — it means adding purposeful structural elements that signal rigour. Starting point: add background grid lines to charts (see DESIGN-02).

Type: Design improvement | Priority: High | Area: All pages / global

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-02] Add background grid lines to Metrics & KPI charts
description:
The metrics and KPI tiles on the Performance Overview have no background grid or reference lines. Charts feel bare and imprecise.

Proposed fix: Add subtle background grid lines to charts on the Metrics & KPI tiles. Grid lines should represent meaningful time intervals — months or weeks are the right interval. Days would be too granular. The grid should be light and secondary — not competing with the data lines — but present enough to make the chart feel structured and analytical.

Design reference: Most professional BI and data tools (Looker, Amplitude, Supermetrics) use light grid lines as a baseline.

Type: Design improvement | Priority: High | Area: Performance Overview → Metrics & KPIs

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-03] Change Target Range line colour from light blue to green
description:
In the Predictive Models charts (e.g. Cost per Acquisition chart for ClassPass), there are currently two blue lines: Deep blue = Business as Usual (cost per acquisition) and Light blue = Target Range. The light blue target range line is barely visible and semantically confusing.

Proposed fix: Change the Target Range line colour from light blue to green. Rationale: Green is conventionally associated with targets, goals, and positive performance benchmarks. It provides clear visual separation from the business-as-usual line and is immediately intuitive without requiring legend reading.

Type: Design improvement | Priority: High | Area: Performance Overview → Predictive Models

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-04] Rename right-hand attribution column on Sources/Media Partners page
description:
The right-hand attribution column on the Sources / Media Partners page does not clearly communicate that the values shown are AIM MMM estimates — not last-touch attribution figures.

Proposed fix: Rename the column to 'AIM Attribution' or equivalent wording that makes clear these are MMM model estimates.

Type: Design improvement | Priority: Medium | Area: Sources / Media Partners

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-03] Add Most/Least Efficient Media Sources summary chart to Performance Overview
description:
The Performance Overview currently doesn't give the client an at-a-glance summary of which channels are performing and which aren't. The user must drill into individual channel views to understand this.

Proposed addition: Add a summary chart near the top of the Performance Overview showing Most efficient media sources (top N channels by efficiency score / marginal ROAS) and Least efficient media sources (bottom N channels — likely over-invested).

Design options: Horizontal bar chart ranked highest to lowest; Two-column card layout — top 3 most efficient / bottom 3 least efficient; Colour coding — green (efficient), amber (watch), red (over-invested).

NOTE: This is exploratory. Discuss with Robert whether the model produces the right efficiency signal to power this simply and reliably. Do not design this until the data output is confirmed.

Type: New feature | Priority: Medium (idea — needs data validation) | Area: Performance Overview → top of page

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-04] Add efficiency / marginal CPA signal to Sources/Media Partners page
description:
The Sources / Media Partners page currently shows attribution data on the right-hand side. In AIM X this will be replaced. For AIM Pro, the left-hand side should also show whether the client is efficient on each channel relative to their media mix.

Proposed fix: Add an efficiency / marginal CPA signal to the left-hand side of the page showing whether the client is over-invested, efficient, or under-invested on each channel.

Type: New feature | Priority: High | Area: Sources / Media Partners

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-05] Add health warning tooltip on AIM Attribution column
description:
The attribution estimates shown in the AIM Attribution column may be misinterpreted by clients as precise figures rather than model estimates.

Proposed fix: Add a health warning tooltip on the AIM Attribution column with text such as: 'These are estimates. Do not treat as certainties.' The tooltip should appear on hover over the column header.

Type: Design improvement | Priority: Medium | Area: Sources / Media Partners

Implementation notes: Use a standard drag handle icon on the left or top-left of each tile. Order should persist after save. Consider a subtle 'drag to reorder' tooltip on first use.

Type: New feature | Priority: High | Area: Performance Overview

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-06] Cost curve charts look too lightweight — needs more visual rigour
description:
The cost curve charts do not visually convey the scientific credibility and analytical depth of the underlying model. Feedback: 'like a PowerPoint presentation.'

Proposed fix: Improve the visual design of cost curve charts to increase perceived analytical rigour. This does not mean adding unnecessary complexity — it means the charts should feel like they belong in a professional data science product, not a slide deck. Specific improvements TBD in design review.

Type: Design improvement | Priority: High | Area: Cost Curve

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-05] Reframe attribution column copy — make clear these are directional MMM estimates, not LTA comparisons
description:
The current attribution column framing is causing client friction. Clients are comparing AIM attribution figures directly against last-touch attribution (LTA) figures from their MMP, which leads to confusion and loss of confidence in the model.

Proposed fix: Reframe all copy and tooltips in the attribution column to make clear that these are directional MMM estimates — not a like-for-like comparison with LTA. This is a copy and tooltip fix — not a data change.

NOTE: This is causing active client friction now. Priority item.

Type: New feature (copy/UX) | Priority: CRITICAL | Area: Sources / Media Partners

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-02] Add model health and provenance signals to Performance Overview (MAPE, last updated, last attribution run)
description:
The Performance Overview currently shows outputs but no information about the model that generated them. Clients have no visibility into how accurate the model is, when it was last updated, or when attribution data was last run.

Proposed additions — add the following contextual signals to the Performance Overview header or model info panel:
- MAPE Score: The model's Mean Absolute Percentage Error — displayed alongside the date it was calculated
- Model Last Updated: Date and time the model was last rebuilt/retrained
- Last Attribution Run: Date and time of the most recent attribution data run

Example format: 'Model accuracy (MAPE): 8.4% (calculated 28 Apr 2026) | Last model update: 29 Apr 2026 14:32 | Last attribution run: 30 Apr 2026 09:17'

These are read-only provenance indicators that materially increase client confidence and reduce 'is this fresh?' support questions.

Type: New feature | Priority: High | Area: Performance Overview → header

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-06] Add persistent active filter display bar to all pages — cadence and lookback window
description:
Users have no at-a-glance view of which filters are currently applied. After selecting cadence and lookback window there is no persistent on-screen indicator.

PROPOSED SOLUTION:
Add a persistent filter bar near the top of all pages showing active filters as labelled pill/chip buttons.

Example:
[ Monthly ] [ Last 12 Months ] [ All Platforms ] [ All Networks ]

Design requirements:
- Pill/chip button style — not plain text
- Each chip clearly labelled with its current value
- Clicking a chip opens the relevant filter selector inline
- Updates immediately when filters change
- Must include at minimum: cadence + lookback window. Platform and network filters should also appear here.

Type: New feature | Priority: High | Area: Global — all pages, specifically Performance Overview and Media Partners
Reported by: Gary Danks — 6 May 2026

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-07] Redesign date filter UX — split into two explicit selectors + reduce calendar to icon
description:
The current date filter UI is unclear. The full calendar button takes up too much space and the relationship between cadence and lookback window is not obvious.

PROPOSED REDESIGN:

1. CADENCE SELECTOR — segmented toggle:
   Monthly | Weekly | Custom

2. LOOKBACK WINDOW SELECTOR — adjacent dropdown or segmented selector showing options relevant to the selected cadence:
   - Monthly: Last 12 Months | Last 9 Months | Last 6 Months | Custom Range
   - Weekly: Last 52 Weeks | Last 26 Weeks | Last 13 Weeks | Custom Range
   - Custom: Custom Range only

3. CALENDAR — reduce to a small calendar icon. When clicked, opens the existing calendar overlay (same behaviour as today, smaller trigger). Only needed for custom date range selection.

This is a UI redesign only — no change to underlying date logic or data.

Combined with FEATURE-06 (persistent filter bar), the user will always know exactly what they are looking at.

Type: New feature / UX redesign | Priority: High | Area: Global — date filter / cadence selector
Reported by: Gary Danks — 6 May 2026

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-09] Recommendations / Optimizer — Add optimizer summary header with KPI target and last run date
description:
The Recommendations section currently lists recommendations with no context about what the optimizer is working towards or when it last ran. Two additions required.

---

CHANGES REQUIRED:

1. OPTIMIZER TARGET SUMMARY
- Add a summary statement at the top of the Recommendations section, above individual recommendation rows
- Must clearly state what KPI the optimizer is currently optimising towards
- Example: 'Currently optimising towards: Paid Subscriptions'
- Must be dynamically pulled from the client's model configuration — not hardcoded
- Will differ per client (e.g. 'Subscriptions' for ClassPass, 'First Time Deposits' for fintech, etc.)

2. OPTIMIZER LAST RUN DATE AND TIME
- Display the date and time the optimizer last ran, adjacent to or below the target summary
- Example: 'Optimizer last run: 5 May 2026 at 22:00'
- Must include a timestamp — date alone is not sufficient
- Must be clearly distinguished from the Model Refresh Date (see FEATURE-08)

---

DESIGN INTENT:
- Compact, positioned at top of Recommendations section — first thing user reads before acting on any recommendation
- Should feel like a live system status panel, not a marketing message
- Gives the user confidence that recommendations are current and reflect the latest model run

---

Type: New feature | Priority: High
Area: Recommendations / Optimizer → section header
Reported by: Gary Danks — 6 May 2026

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-08] Performance Overview — Add Model Performance section above Metrics & KPIs
description:
A new 'Model Performance' section is required at the very top of the Performance Overview page, positioned ABOVE the existing Metrics & KPI tiles. This section gives users immediate confidence that their model is live, accurate, and up to date.

---

CONTENT REQUIRED:

1. MAPE SCORE
- Display the current MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error) score
- Show as a colour-coded badge with a performance label:
  • Excellent → Green
  • Good → Yellow-green
  • Standard → Amber
  • Poor → Red
  (Exact thresholds to be confirmed with Robert / Data Science)
- Display the date and time the MAPE was recorded alongside the score
- MAPE updates daily — show today's date if available. If not, must be no more than 7 days ago.

2. MODEL REFRESH DATE
- Date and time the model was last rebuilt / retrained
- Target: within last 7 days
- Format: 'Last refreshed: 5 May 2026 at 14:32'

3. LAST ATTRIBUTION RUN
- Date and time of the most recent attribution data run
- Runs daily — should reflect the most recent run
- Format: 'Last attribution run: 6 May 2026 at 09:17'

---

DESIGN INTENT:
- Must look scientific and data-driven — feels like it is pulled live from the backend
- Conveys recency and freshness — user should feel their model is current and active
- MAPE badge colour must be immediately legible without reading the label
- Do not use decorative or marketing-style design — this is a technical provenance panel

---

Type: New feature | Priority: High
Area: Performance Overview → top of page, above Metrics & KPIs
Reported by: Gary Danks — 6 May 2026

title: [MMM] [UX-05] Media Partners — Column headers do not stick when scrolling, making table unusable
description:
In the Media Partners section, the table column headers (e.g. Media Partner, Ad Network, Spend, etc.) scroll out of view as the user scrolls down the table. Once the headers disappear, the user has no way to identify which column they are looking at — making the table very difficult to use, especially for clients with many networks.

STEPS TO REPRODUCE:
1. Navigate to Media Partners
2. View the table with multiple networks listed
3. Scroll down the table

ACTUAL RESULT:

- User loses all column context when scrolling through data

EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR:

- This is standard behaviour for any data table — the header row should never scroll out of view
- Sticky header must apply across all columns in the Media Partners table

This is a usability issue affecting all clients with more than a small number of networks in their media mix.

Area: Media Partners → main table → column headers

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-01] Overall visual language feels too lightweight — all pages
description:
The current AIM Insights interface is too clean and minimal. It does not visually convey the sophistication of the underlying Bayesian model. Clients who see it for the first time may not appreciate the level of statistical rigour behind the outputs.

Proposed fix: Review the overall visual design with the goal of increasing perceived analytical depth. This does not mean adding clutter — it means adding purposeful structural elements that signal rigour. Starting point: add background grid lines to charts (see DESIGN-02).

Type: Design improvement | Priority: High | Area: All pages / global

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-02] Add background grid lines to Metrics & KPI charts
description:
The metrics and KPI tiles on the Performance Overview have no background grid or reference lines. Charts feel bare and imprecise.

Proposed fix: Add subtle background grid lines to charts on the Metrics & KPI tiles. Grid lines should represent meaningful time intervals — months or weeks are the right interval. Days would be too granular. The grid should be light and secondary — not competing with the data lines — but present enough to make the chart feel structured and analytical.

Design reference: Most professional BI and data tools (Looker, Amplitude, Supermetrics) use light grid lines as a baseline.

Type: Design improvement | Priority: High | Area: Performance Overview → Metrics & KPIs

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-03] Change Target Range line colour from light blue to green
description:
In the Predictive Models charts (e.g. Cost per Acquisition chart for ClassPass), there are currently two blue lines: Deep blue = Business as Usual (cost per acquisition) and Light blue = Target Range. The light blue target range line is barely visible and semantically confusing.

Proposed fix: Change the Target Range line colour from light blue to green. Rationale: Green is conventionally associated with targets, goals, and positive performance benchmarks. It provides clear visual separation from the business-as-usual line and is immediately intuitive without requiring legend reading.

Type: Design improvement | Priority: High | Area: Performance Overview → Predictive Models

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-04] Rename right-hand attribution column on Sources/Media Partners page
description:
The right-hand attribution column on the Sources / Media Partners page does not clearly communicate that the values shown are AIM MMM estimates — not last-touch attribution figures.

Proposed fix: Rename the column to 'AIM Attribution' or equivalent wording that makes clear these are MMM model estimates.

Type: Design improvement | Priority: Medium | Area: Sources / Media Partners

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-03] Add Most/Least Efficient Media Sources summary chart to Performance Overview
description:
The Performance Overview currently doesn't give the client an at-a-glance summary of which channels are performing and which aren't. The user must drill into individual channel views to understand this.

Proposed addition: Add a summary chart near the top of the Performance Overview showing Most efficient media sources (top N channels by efficiency score / marginal ROAS) and Least efficient media sources (bottom N channels — likely over-invested).

Design options: Horizontal bar chart ranked highest to lowest; Two-column card layout — top 3 most efficient / bottom 3 least efficient; Colour coding — green (efficient), amber (watch), red (over-invested).

NOTE: This is exploratory. Discuss with Robert whether the model produces the right efficiency signal to power this simply and reliably. Do not design this until the data output is confirmed.

Type: New feature | Priority: Medium (idea — needs data validation) | Area: Performance Overview → top of page

title: [MMM] [FEATURE-04] Add efficiency / marginal CPA signal to Sources/Media Partners page
description:
The Sources / Media Partners page currently shows attribution data on the right-hand side. In AIM X this will be replaced. For AIM Pro, the left-hand side should also show whether the client is efficient on each channel relative to their media mix.

Proposed fix: Add an efficiency / marginal CPA signal to the left-hand side of the page showing whether the client is over-invested, efficient, or under-invested on each channel.

Type: New feature | Priority: High | Area: Sources / Media Partners

title: [MMM] [DESIGN-05] Add health warning tooltip on AIM Attribution column
description:
The attribution estimates shown in the AIM Attribution column may be misinterpreted by clients as precise figures rather than model estimates.

Proposed fix: Add a health warning tooltip on the AIM Attribution column with text such as: 'These are estimates. Do not treat as certainties.' The tooltip should appear on hover over the column header.

Type: Design improvement | Priority: Medium | Area: Sources / Media Partners

title: Scenario Planner QA — Default media sources to active networks only instead of showing all historical networks as enabled
description:
Summary:
The Media Sources step currently appears to show all historical client networks, resulting in a very long active set such as 75/75 selected. This is unrealistic for typical scenario planning.

Problem:
Users generally do not want to include every network ever used over years of history. Showing all historical networks as effectively active by default creates noise and unnecessary cleanup.

Observed behaviour:
- Media Sources displayed 75 out of 75
- This appears to reflect all networks ever used by the client across several years of historical data
- This is unrealistic for present-day scenario planning

Suggested fix:
- Default the active/selected state to currently active networks only
- Show inactive/historical networks as off by default, while still allowing users to turn them on if needed
- Keep active selections visible as blue pills on the right-hand side, with historical/inactive sources switched off initially

Steps to reproduce:
1. Go to Media Sources for a client with long history
2. Observe large all-time network count and active set (example: 75/75)
3. Note that many of these are likely stale/historical rather than current planning inputs

Expected behaviour:
- Currently active networks are enabled by default
- Historical/inactive networks are off by default but still available

Actual behaviour:
- All historical networks appear to be included, creating unrealistic defaults

Acceptance criteria:
- Default selection reflects active/current networks only
- Historical/inactive networks are available but off by default
- Media source list is easier to manage for realistic scenario setup

Priority: High

Scenario Planner QA — Fix budget toggle visual state and require valid budget input before progressing
description:
Summary:
The budget step has both visual-state and validation issues. Weekly/monthly toggle styling is unclear in the ON state, and the flow allows users to proceed without selecting a budget mode or entering a budget amount.

Problem:
The toggle loses clarity when enabled, and required budget input is not enforced.

Observed behaviour:
- When weekly/monthly buttons are turned on, the circular button inside the pill disappears and the control becomes all blue
- This makes ON state unclear compared with other toggles in the UI
- The user can move forward without selecting weekly or monthly budget
- The user can also move forward without entering a budget amount

Why this matters:
- Weakens clarity of a critical setup step
- Allows incomplete scenario configuration
- Increases likelihood of downstream errors or confusing defaults

Suggested fix:
- Update ON-state styling to match the clearer pattern used elsewhere, e.g. white button on blue background or consistent grey/off blue/on pill treatment
- Enforce required validation so the user cannot continue without:
  - selecting weekly or monthly mode
  - entering a valid budget amount

Steps to reproduce:
1. Go to Budget step
2. Toggle weekly/monthly and observe unclear active styling
3. Attempt to continue without selecting a budget mode and/or without entering a budget
4. Observe that progression is allowed

Expected behaviour:
- Toggle state is visually clear
- User cannot progress without valid budget configuration

Actual behaviour:
- Toggle state is visually weak and progression is allowed with incomplete input

Acceptance criteria:
- Weekly/monthly controls have clear ON/OFF states
- Budget type selection is required
- Budget amount is required before progressing

Priority: Critical

title: Scenario Planner QA — Review scenario creation IA: merge “Create” and “Select Apps” into a single step or clearer unified flow
description:
Summary:
The scenario creation flow currently separates naming/description from app selection, but the user experience suggests these belong together.

Problem:
From a workflow perspective, naming a scenario, describing it, and choosing which app(s) it applies to feel like one creation action. Splitting them into separate steps adds friction.

Observed behaviour:
- User enters scenario name and description in the Create a New Scenario section
- App selection happens in a separate Select Apps step
- This feels like unnecessary separation of a single conceptual action

Why this matters:
- Makes creation feel more fragmented than necessary
- Increases steps for a simple mental model: “create a scenario for these apps”

Suggested fix:
- Review whether scenario metadata and app selection can be merged into one step
- If not merged, improve the information architecture so it feels like one continuous creation action

Steps to reproduce:
1. Start creating a new scenario
2. Enter scenario name and description
3. Proceed to Select Apps
4. Observe that this feels like an artificial split in the flow

Expected behaviour:
- Creation flow should match user mental model and minimise unnecessary steps

Actual behaviour:
- Metadata entry and app selection are separated in a way that feels unintuitive

Acceptance criteria:
- Product/design team reviews whether the two steps should be merged
- If kept separate, the flow is reframed to feel more cohesive and intentional

Priority: Medium
Type: UX improvement / design review

title: Scenario Planner QA — Review multi-step scenario creation UX for a future single-page configurator flow
description:
Summary:
As a phase-three design direction, scenario creation may work better as a single-page configurator with a persistent summary rather than a rigid stepped flow.

Problem:
The current step-based flow can force users to think of dependent choices too late, causing backtracking.

Observed behaviour:
- During scenario creation, the user encountered decisions later in the flow that made them want to revisit earlier steps
- The stepped experience did not feel fully intuitive

Suggested future improvement:
- Explore a one-page scenario configurator
- Allow users to build the scenario while seeing a live summary/update panel as they move through the configuration
- Reduce need for backward navigation when dependent choices become clearer later

Expected benefit:
- Stronger sense of configurator workflow
- Better visibility of all selected settings at once
- Fewer back-and-forth corrections

Acceptance criteria:
- Logged as phase-three UX/design exploration item
- Design review considers single-page configurator with persistent summary

Priority: Low
Type: Future enhancement / UX exploration

title: [BUG-SP-13] Scenario Planner — No edit functionality on active scenarios
description:
Area: Scenario Planner → Active scenario management
Type: New feature / Bug
Priority: Medium

Problem:
Once a scenario is activated, the edit button is grayed out / unavailable. This means if a client needs to update their budget mid-month (e.g. offline media budget is cut, or a new trading deal requires spend reallocation), they must deactivate the scenario and recreate it from scratch. In a mid-month scenario, this requires manual calculation of remaining budget — a significant overhead.

Expected behaviour: Active scenarios should be editable. Clients should be able to update specific fields (network min/max, budget values) on an active scenario, with the optimizer re-running automatically on save.

Actual behaviour: Edit button grayed out / locked while scenario is active.

Note: It is unclear whether deactivating a scenario and recreating it mid-month is the intended workflow or an oversight. Please confirm intended behaviour before fixing.

Reported by: Gary Danks + Guillermo Martinez — Optimiser Training session, 12 June 2026

title: [BUG-SP-10] Scenario Planner — Flexible budget target CPA currency appears hardcoded to USD
description:
Area: Scenario Planner → Flexible budget → Target CPA field
Type: Bug fix
Priority: P1 — Critical

Problem:
The target CPA field in the Flexible budget option appears to display USD regardless of the client's configured account currency. De Facto's account is configured in Turkish Lira (TRY) — if the field is hardcoded to USD, clients entering CPA targets in their local currency will be submitting incorrect values without knowing.

Expected behaviour: The target CPA field currency must reflect the client's configured account currency (e.g. TRY for De Facto, EUR for European accounts).
Actual behaviour: Currency appears as USD regardless of account configuration.

Note: This issue is likely present throughout the Scenario Planner, not just in the flexible budget CPA field. Rhiannon noted the dashboard also appears in USD when De Facto is configured in TRY. This may be a wider currency rendering bug.

description:

title: [BUG-SP-07] Scenario Planner — Scenario tile shows no budget detail or constraint summary
description:
Area: Scenario Planner → Scenario tile
Type: UX improvement
Priority: Medium

Problem:
Scenario tiles currently only display the scenario name, strategy, and whether the budget type is "Fixed" or "Flexible". They do not show the actual budget amounts, active constraints, or which networks have been turned off or capped. This means clients returning to a scenario later (e.g. the following day) cannot quickly recall what configuration they set.

Expected behaviour: Scenario tile should display:
- Total budget (monthly summary if weekly input)
- Weekly vs monthly budget type indicator
- Any active constraints (networks turned off, min/max values set)
- Creator + date

Actual behaviour: Only shows name, strategy type, and Fixed/Flexible label.

Reported by: Gary Danks — Optimiser Training session, 12 June 2026
Quote: "There needs to be more detail in that tile. It needs to say who created it, what the budget is, any constraints."

title: [BUG-SP-01] Scenario Planner — Fixed / Flexible budget type can be multi-selected
description:
Area: Scenario Planner → Budget step
Type: Bug fix
Priority: P1 — Critical

Problem:
Both "Fixed" and "Flexible" budget options can be selected simultaneously. They should be mutually exclusive — only one should be selectable at a time.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Navigate to Scenario Planner → create new scenario
2. Reach the budget type step
3. Select "Fixed" — then also select "Flexible"
4. Both remain selected — no deselect occurs

Expected behaviour: Selecting one option should deselect the other (radio button behaviour).
Actual behaviour: Both can be selected simultaneously.

Source: projects/transcripts/2026-06-12-optimiser-training-rhia-guillermo.md

title: [BUG-SP-12] Scenario Planner — Activation confirmation card lacks scenario summary
description:
Area: Scenario Planner → Activation confirmation modal
Type: UX improvement
Priority: Medium

Problem:
When a client clicks Activate on a scenario, a confirmation card appears but it does not include a meaningful summary of what is being activated. If the scenario was created the day before or by a different team member, the client may not remember its configuration and is being asked to confirm something they cannot verify.

Expected behaviour: Activation confirmation modal should display a full summary of the scenario:
- Strategy and goal
- Budget type (fixed/flexible) and total budget amount
- Key constraints (networks turned off, min/max values)
- App / model the scenario applies to

Fix for this could be a summary option where the user presses the summary button and a pop-up with a full summary of the scenario appears with an activation button. 

Actual behaviour: Confirmation card shown with minimal detail.

Reported by: Gary Danks — Optimiser Training session, 12 June 2026
